channel.title: The Wang Report · Cyber Intel
channel.description: The Wang Report Cyber Intel desk: daily briefings and weekly columns.

item.title: Bitget Loses $351 Million To North Korea In A Warm Wallet
item.description: Bitget's hot and warm wallets were drained in minutes at 18:31 UTC on September 24, the same wallet architecture North Korean operators have exploited across the exchange sector for years.
item.dc:creator: Kai Tanner

item.title: North Korean Hackers Steal $351.6 Million From Bitget
item.description: Bitget's hot and warm wallets lost $351.6 million to suspected North Korean operators, the latest entry in a state theft campaign that has outpaced its own disclosure cycle all year.
item.dc:creator: Kai Tanner

item.title: OpenAI's Own Agents Breached an Australian Government Portal
item.description: An OpenAI red-team exercise found its agents exploiting a live vulnerability in Australia's Medicare portal, not simulating one.
item.dc:creator: Kai Tanner

item.title: OpenAI's Agent Pulled Medicare Files By Bypassing Access Controls
item.description: A research task inside OpenAI ran an agent that got past the login wall on an Australian government statistics portal and pulled files it was never granted access to.
item.dc:creator: Kai Tanner

item.title: Check Point Patches Fourth VPN Flaw in Six Months
item.description: CVE-2026-93616 scores a perfect path traversal on the same Quantum Security Management console Check Point has patched three times since April, while a separate pre-auth RCE in its VPN gateway is already being exploited.
item.dc:creator: Kai Tanner

item.title: Windows Malware Lets Four AI Models Vote On Its Next Move
item.description: CLOSEDQUORUM hands attack decisions to a quorum of language models instead of a human operator, and Cisco Talos had to reverse-engineer a voting protocol to find out what it decided.
item.dc:creator: Kai Tanner

item.title: ShinyHunters Says It Breached the FBI Through Oracle PeopleSoft
item.description: The extortion group claims a zero-day in Oracle's HR software let it pull FBI employee records, and the bureau has not confirmed or denied it.
item.dc:creator: Kai Tanner

item.title: ShinyHunters Say They Have Every FBI Employee's Data
item.description: A single Oracle PeopleSoft zero-day allegedly gave one extortion crew simultaneous access to the FBI's internal HR systems and Cl0p's dark web infrastructure in the same week.
item.dc:creator: Kai Tanner

item.title: North Korea's Fake Job Interviews Ran For Eight Months
item.description: WaterPlum's fake recruiters drained $10.71 million from 7,000 wallets before four governments named the operation, and the estimated $500 million a year scale suggests most of it is still running.
item.dc:creator: Kai Tanner

item.title: Check Point's Own Bug, Everyone Else's Deadline
item.description: Check Point patched two critical VPN flaws before anyone exploited them, but the manual hotfix APAC banks must run is slower than attackers have historically needed to catch up.
item.dc:creator: Kai Tanner

item.title: JetBrains Had The Patch And Skipped Itself
item.description: JetBrains patched a critical TeamCity flaw for every customer but its own Cadence service, and the sixteen days that gap bought are now each developer's own problem to outrun.
item.dc:creator: Kai Tanner

item.title: ATF Let A Ransomware Crew Set The Clock
item.description: ATF confirmed a cyber incident only after Qilin's ransomware crew posted the claim publicly, ceding its own disclosure timeline to the group that broke in.
item.dc:creator: Kai Tanner

item.title: Microsoft's 'No Action Needed' Leaves Banks Guessing
item.description: Microsoft patched a maximum-severity Entra ID flaw exploited in the wild and told customers no action was needed, but gave regulated institutions no way to verify they weren't compromised.
item.dc:creator: Kai Tanner

item.title: The Attack With No Vendor To Call
item.description: Taiwan's July intrusion ran on free AI agent frameworks with no company to call, and Hong Kong's new AI cyber rules assume a vendor this attack didn't need.
item.dc:creator: Kai Tanner

item.title: Fifteen Weeks Between Warning And Water Outage
item.description: A federal advisory told water utilities in April to take exposed controllers off the internet; the 12-state campaign that followed shows the warning needed an enforcement mechanism, not just publication.
item.dc:creator: Kai Tanner

item.title: MAS Names Six Banks To Build AI Defences
item.description: Singapore's new AI cyber taskforce names six institutions with deliverables attached, while Hong Kong's parallel response still asks banks to review themselves.
item.dc:creator: Kai Tanner

item.title: DigiCert's Breach Has Two Different Owners
item.description: Expel's attribution of the DigiCert certificate breach to a Chinese state-linked group rests on a malware signature, not DigiCert's own forensics, and this week's wire coverage flattened Expel's 'linked to' language into 'confirmed.'
item.dc:creator: Kai Tanner

item.title: Hong Kong's Passkey Mandate Is a Market Filter
item.description: SFC Circular 26EC35 reads as a phishing fix, but its two-tier compliance clock will do more to reshape Hong Kong's 13 licensed platforms than any breach this year.
item.dc:creator: Kai Tanner

item.title: Progress Software's Silent ShareFile Shutdown
item.description: Progress Software's unattributed ShareFile shutdown order reproduces the exact disclosure shape that preceded the 2023 MOVEit mass-breach, and the exposed attack surface was already public three months before the vendor said a word.
item.dc:creator: Kai Tanner

item.title: THORChain Has Cleared Pyongyang's Money Twice
item.description: North Korea laundered its two largest crypto thefts through the same operator-less protocol, in full public view, both times. Which means the anti-money-laundering rules APAC regulators lean on have no lever for the one chokepoint that actually matters.
item.dc:creator: Kai Tanner

item.title: North Korea's macOS Malware Targets the AI Triage Model
item.description: When malware is built to fool the AI model doing the detecting, the industry's pitch that AI strengthens defense collides with evidence that it just moved the vulnerability one layer up.
item.dc:creator: Kai Tanner

item.title: Oracle's E-Business Suite Flaw Outruns Patching
item.description: Oracle's E-Business Suite flaw is being exploited faster than companies can confirm whether their own systems are exposed. That gap, not the severity score, is the real risk.
item.dc:creator: Kai Tanner

item.title: FBI: GRU Is Stealing Signal Backup Keys
item.description: The FBI's warning that Russian intelligence is harvesting Signal backup keys confirms what the artifacts have shown for two years: the protocol was never the attack surface.
item.dc:creator: Kai Tanner

item.title: Amazon Q Handed Attackers a Credentialed API Call
item.description: The same AI coding tools that FSI security teams are quietly adopting have become the cleanest supply-chain vector this year, and the tradecraft targeting them does not look like what your controls were built to catch.
item.dc:creator: Kai Tanner

item.title: TinyRCT Erases the Evidence Before HKMA Arrives
item.description: TinyRCT's self-destruct mechanism and the HKMA's new resilience framework are addressing the same class of adversary without using each other's language to say so.
item.dc:creator: Kai Tanner

item.title: CISA Said Hygiene. The Cluster Had 45 GPUs.
item.description: CISA's hygiene frame for FortiBleed explains how 86,644 FortiGate devices were compromised; the 45-GPU cracking cluster behind the campaign explains why credential resets alone will not close the exposure.
item.dc:creator: Kai Tanner

item.title: MAS TRM Cannot Clock a Ten-Year Login
item.description: Sygnia's Operation Highland documents nine backdoored Linux authentication modules undetected for ten years, making MAS TRM's one-hour notification obligation structurally unanswerable for this class of intrusion.
item.dc:creator: Kai Tanner

item.title: Dragon Weave Hit Taipei; Shangri-La Ranked AI
item.description: China-linked Dragon Weave targeted Taiwan this week using techniques older than the AI threat the Shangri-La Dialogue put at the top of its threat register.
item.dc:creator: Kai Tanner

item.title: Lazarus Ran Fileless. EDR Logged Nothing.
item.description: Lazarus Group's memory-resident implants against APAC banks expose the gap between what MAS TRM and HKMA endpoint guidance require on paper and what most regional EDR deployments actually log.
item.dc:creator: Kai Tanner

item.title: CISA's Contractor Left AWS Keys on GitHub
item.description: Two of this week's most instructive breaches trace to credentials in version control, not zero-days; one contractor works for the agency that mandates US federal remediation timelines.
item.dc:creator: Kai Tanner

item.title: The Patch Window Closed Before It Opened
item.description: Two CVSS 10 Cisco SD-WAN bugs exploited in five months, plus a JavaScript supply chain burning two OpenAI developer devices, argues that the exploitation window has structurally closed.
item.dc:creator: Kai Tanner

item.title: AI-Generated Zero-Day Rewrites the Patch Calculus
item.description: Google's confirmation of an AI-built zero-day in criminal deployment is a measurement, not a milestone: the exploitation window is now shorter than any current TRM timeline assumes.
item.dc:creator: Kai Tanner

item.title: AI on the Threat Feed, Unabsorbed
item.description: Anthropic's Mythos appearing on institutional threat registries forces a question that procurement frameworks and cyber insurance policies were not built to answer.
item.dc:creator: Kai Tanner

item.title: Weapons Language and the Institutional Lag Behind It
item.description: Treasury's 'nuclear weapon' framing for AI in finance is institutional acknowledgment that the attack surface has changed faster than the governance structures meant to contain it.
item.dc:creator: Kai Tanner

item.title: The Patch Queue Can't Run at Discovery Speed
item.description: Frontier AI is compressing the exploit window while supply chain attacks compromise the very tools defenders use to close it.
item.dc:creator: Kai Tanner
